next_steps: Load and apply the local skill-refiner gate before any rewrite.
Ask the user to define the Skill's intended owner/domain, primary users, concrete workflows, and what current consumers depend on.
If the intended domain cannot be stated, route to skill-creator/discovery to define or split the skill instead of refining an unclear mixed-domain Skill.
Keep this as a decision-only dry run; make no file edits.
risk_notes: A direct 'best practice rewrite' would be premature because the domain boundary is unknown.
Mixed-domain behavior suggests the real problem may be skill decomposition or new skill creation, not refinement.
Without consumer and success criteria context, edits could break existing users or optimize toward the wrong responsibility.
reason_summary: The next gate is clarification/ownership, not implementation. Skill-refiner should not force a rewrite when the Skill's responsibility is unclear and cross-domain; the honest move is to pause for domain and consumer context, then route to skill-creator if the work is actually definition/splitting rather than refining an established Skill.
